::: {.callout-important title="Play first"}
Finish the three levels and make one small code change. Then move to the Life Checkpoint assignment.
:::

## Open the game

### Fastest method

1. Click **[PLAY CIRCUIT QUEST IN JUPYTERLITE](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/index.html?fromURL=https%3A%2F%2Fandrewandrade.ca%2Ftech-edu-resources%2Fassets%2Ftej-computational%2Fnotebooks%2F09a-circuit-quest.ipynb){target="_blank"}**.
2. Choose **Python (Pyodide)** if Jupyter asks for a kernel.
3. Run the setup cell.
4. Change the team name and one colour in **Make it yours**.
5. Run the play cell and finish all three levels.

### Download and upload method

If the direct link does not open the notebook:

1. Download [Circuit Quest (`.ipynb`)](../../assets/tej-computational/notebooks/09a-circuit-quest.ipynb).
2. Open **[JupyterLite](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/){target="_blank"}**.
3. Select **Upload Files** and choose `09a-circuit-quest.ipynb`.
4. Double-click the uploaded file and choose **Python (Pyodide)**.

## What to do

1. Change `TEAM_NAME`.
2. Change one colour word. Try `hotpink`, `orange`, `violet`, `gold`, `cyan`, or `lime`.
3. Run the play cell.
4. Click a wire tile to rotate it. Connected tiles glow green.
5. Light every lamp. Use **Hint** or **Reset level** if needed.

The game contains three small levels:

| Level | Goal |
|---|---|
| 1. One turn to power | Rotate one wire and light one lamp. |
| 2. Route around the corner | Build a complete path through a 3 by 3 grid. |
| 3. Power two lamps | Rotate a junction and power two branches. |

::: {.callout-note title="Your code is part of the game"}
The game displays the team name and colours you put in the code. Leave the collapsed game engine alone for now.
:::

## What happens next

Circuit Quest is the warm-up. **Do not rebuild the tile board in Tinkercad.**

1. Open the [Life Checkpoint Upgrade instructions](midterm-circuit-investigation.qmd).
2. Open the Life Checkpoint notebook and correct the checkpoint work in Jupyter.
3. Build the checkpoint's two-loop circuit in Tinkercad: $12\,\mathrm{V}$ and $5\,\mathrm{V}$ sources with $5\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$, $7\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$, and $2\,\mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistors.
4. Compare the Tinkercad currents with the Python answers.

**[OPEN THE LIFE CHECKPOINT ASSIGNMENT](midterm-circuit-investigation.qmd)**

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| No board appears | Run the setup, team-and-colours, and play cells in order. |
| Buttons appear as plain text | Select **Python (Pyodide)** as the kernel. |
| A lamp stays off | Follow the green path and rotate the first blue tile after it. |
| You cannot find the mistake | Select **Hint**. |
| You want to start over | Select **Reset level**. |
| The browser was closed | Reopen or upload the notebook and run both game cells again. |

## Source note

The activity adapts the rotating-tile idea used by circuit-path and Netwalk-style puzzles. It uses `ipywidgets`; the setup cell installs it automatically when the browser environment does not already have it. The circuit levels and notebook implementation are original course materials.
